solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Carrier with mouldable catch

parts.note: plastic material can be moulded into shape
to bag game is to catch it

explanation.surface: A carrier fitted with a catch that can be shaped by hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A shopping bag of polythene is a common carrier for goods.

clue.text: Where in France between both sides there is menacing scowl

indicators.note: between says one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: L and R are left and right, both sides
ou is French for where

explanation.surface: Somewhere in France, a threatening frown appears on every side.
explanation.definitionFit: To lour is to frown or look menacing; as a noun it is a scowl.

clue.text: Got rid of all one's stock of drink that's dated inside

definitions.text: Got rid of all one's stock

indicators.note: inside says one piece goes within the other

parts.note: to sup is to drink
old means dated

explanation.surface: A trader cleared out an ageing drinks stock.
explanation.definitionFit: A seller who has sold up has disposed of everything, often a whole business.

clue.text: Having arrived, go energetically heading towards station

parts.note: in means arrived, as a train is in
to bound is to leap energetically

explanation.surface: Arriving after rushing to the station.
explanation.definitionFit: An inbound train is coming in towards its terminus or home station.

clue.text: There's no fighting in fortification that's a huge structure

indicators.note: no says the fighting word is taken out

parts.note: a bulwark is a defensive wall
war is fighting

explanation.surface: Peace reigns in the fort, a vast edifice.
explanation.definitionFit: Bulk can mean a large mass or structure, especially a ship's hull.

clue.text: Pleasant time for formal greeting in Oz?

definitions.meaning: an enjoyable day out is a pleasant time
the full form of the Australian greeting G'day

explanation.surface: Enjoying oneself while saying hello Down Under.
explanation.walkthrough: Oz is Australia, where the greeting is shortened to G'day; the full phrase is its formal version.
explanation.definitionFit: A fine day is pleasant, and the phrase is also a salutation.

clue.text: Display item of clothing for rider

parts.note: to show is to display
a jumper is a knitted sweater, the British word for pullover

explanation.surface: Showing off a sweater meant for horse riding.
explanation.definitionFit: A showjumper is a horse rider competing over fences in an arena.

clue.text: Type of surgery on hospital furnace!

parts.note: open-heart surgery is a kind of operation
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A kind of surgery carried out at a hospital furnace.
explanation.definitionFit: An open-hearth furnace is a type used in steelmaking.

clue.text: Hack composer dropped in

indicators.note: dropped says the word in is taken away from the composer

parts.note: Chopin is the Polish composer

explanation.surface: A hack journalist mentions that a composer called by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropped in' looks like 'paid a visit', but 'dropped' removes IN from CHOPIN.
explanation.definitionFit: To hack at something is to cut it roughly, a synonym.

clue.text: A bear at port first causing uproar

indicators.note: first says the port comes before the rest

parts.note: Hull is a port on the Humber estuary in England
Baloo is the bear in The Jungle Book

explanation.surface: A bear at the harbour is the first to cause a commotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at' is a link; 'first' puts HULL ahead of A and BALOO.
explanation.definitionFit: A noisy commotion or fuss is a synonym for uproar.

clue.text: Incomplete picture contract

indicators.note: Incomplete says the picture word loses its final letter

parts.note: a drawing is a picture

explanation.surface: An unfinished picture is the subject of a business contract.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contract' looks like a noun (an agreement) but is the verb, to shrink.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw in is to pull inward or shrink, as days shorten in autumn.

clue.text: Pre-eminent spinner has only 50% of the game

parts.note: a top is a spinning toy

indicators.note: has only 50% of says only half of the game's name is kept

parts.note: ping-pong is another name for table tennis

explanation.surface: A leading bowler only plays half the match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spinner' suggests a cricket spin bowler, but it is a child's top.
explanation.definitionFit: Topping is British informal for excellent or first-rate.

clue.text: Box set

definitions.meaning: the box is British slang for ...
a TV set is the receiver

explanation.definitionFit: Both words are informal names for the receiver that shows broadcasts.

clue.text: Detective appearing periodically?

definitions.meaning: a periodical: the British satirical magazine issued fortnightly

explanation.walkthrough: Private Eye is a British satirical fortnightly magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: A private detective is called a private eye; the magazine of that name is a periodical.

clue.text: Understand, say, soaring bird

indicators.note: soaring in a down clue says each piece reads upwards

parts.note: eg, for example, is what say means
a tit is a small bird

explanation.surface: Grasp the idea of, for instance, a bird rising up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soaring' turns EG to GE; TIT reads the same either way.
explanation.definitionFit: To get it is idiomatic for to understand.

clue.text: Damage said key shelter

parts.note: to mar is to damage

indicators.note: said signals the next word is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: key is spoken and written as it sounds in the answer

explanation.surface: Harm reported to a crucial refuge.
explanation.definitionFit: A marquee is a large tent used as a shelter at outdoor events.

clue.text: Norma moved house

indicators.note: moved says the letters are shifted about into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Norma has moved house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moved house' reads as relocating, but 'moved' is the anagram signal and 'house' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A manor is a large country house.

clue.text: Last month, one year after producing rot

indicators.note: after places the year at the end

parts.note: December, abbreviated Dec, is the last month of the year
a means one

explanation.surface: Last month, a year later, something began to rot.
explanation.definitionFit: Decay and rot are synonyms for decomposition.

clue.text: See inside joint

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see
in means inside

explanation.surface: Look inside the joint of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: A loin is a cut or joint of meat from the back of an animal.

clue.text: Sister turned up in siding

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside another
turned says the word up is read backwards

explanation.surface: A nun appeared in a railway siding.
explanation.definitionFit: A spur is a short branch line of railway, much like a siding.

clue.text: Lad wrong to include doctor

indicators.note: to include says one piece holds the other

parts.note: a sin is a wrong
MO is Medical Officer, a doctor

explanation.surface: A boy is wrong to bring in a doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: Simon is a boy's name, so a lad is an example.

clue.text: Jeered when old Bob made guttural sounds

parts.note: bob was slang for a shilling, abbreviated s, in old British money

indicators.note: sounds says the word is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: coughed means made a harsh throat noise

explanation.surface: People heckled when an old fellow called Bob cleared his throat.
explanation.walkthrough: A shilling (bob) was a pre-decimal British coin, written s.
explanation.definitionFit: To scoff is to mock, so jeered is a synonym in the past tense.

clue.text: Contradicted Edward holding entrance money

indicators.note: holding says the first piece contains the second

parts.note: Ned is a short form of Edward
the gate is the money taken at the entrance of a sports ground

explanation.surface: Edward denied keeping the admission takings.
explanation.definitionFit: To negate a statement is to deny or contradict it.

clue.text: By way of channel bridge

parts.note: via means by way of
a duct is a channel or pipe

explanation.surface: A bridge reached by way of a channel.
explanation.definitionFit: A viaduct is a long bridge carrying a road or railway across a valley.

clue.text: New awakening concerning one's origin

parts.note: re means about or concerning
birth is one's origin

explanation.surface: A fresh awakening about where one comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebirth is a revival or renaissance, a new awakening.

clue.text: Partly skimp airing leading to damage

indicators.note: Partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Cutting back on ventilation can cause harm.
explanation.definitionFit: To impair is to weaken or damage; 'leading to' is a link.

clue.text: Get official reprimand

parts.note: to get something is to understand or see it
off is an abbreviation of official

explanation.surface: Receive an official telling-off.
explanation.walkthrough: To see someone off is chiefly British slang for to reprimand them.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang verb phrase: to see off is to scold or tell off, per Chambers.

clue.text: Fish hung up, salted initially before first smoke appeared

indicators.note: initially says the opening letters of those words are taken
first says the opening letter of smoke is taken

explanation.surface: Fish was hung up and salted before being smoked.
explanation.definitionFit: Huss is a British name for dogfish sold as food.

clue.text: From Zambia, set off with gusto

parts.note: Z is the international vehicle code for Zambia

indicators.note: off says the letters are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: Someone from Zambia sets off enthusiastically.
explanation.definitionFit: Zest and gusto both mean keen enjoyment.

clue.text: Fellow with reddish-brown coat reckoned to have hindered

parts.note: rust is a reddish-brown coating on iron
rated means reckoned or judged

explanation.surface: A man in a reddish-brown coat was thought to have been obstructive.
explanation.definitionFit: To be thwarted or held back is synonymous with being hindered.

clue.text: Only ten, not fifty getting precious stone

indicators.note: not says the letter for fifty is removed from the word only

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: Only ten, not fifty, end up with a gem.
explanation.definitionFit: Onyx is a banded variety of chalcedony used as a semi-precious gemstone.

clue.text: Desire data about much-wanted poem

indicators.note: about signals the letters are turned around into a new order

explanation.surface: Wanting information about a sought-after poem.
explanation.walkthrough: Desiderata means things much wanted and is also Max Ehrmann's well-known prose poem.
explanation.definitionFit: Desiderata, Latin for things desired, is the title of a famous inspirational poem.
